headline: Police defuse bomb hidden in umbrella near Motijheel Metro Rail Station
summary: An improvised explosive device (IED) was found and neutralized by the CTTC bomb disposal team on Friday evening.
details: A bomb-like object, identified as an improvised explosive device (IED), was discovered beneath the Motijheel Metro Rail Station in Dhaka on Friday evening.
The device was hidden inside a red umbrella, designed to explode when the button was pressed. The CTTC bomb disposal team of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) neutralized the device.
Ansar members on duty at the metro station noticed the umbrella lying on the road near Shapla Chattar during a Rath Yatra procession.
Upon picking up the umbrella, Ansar members saw a red light flashing inside it, which immediately alerted them to the danger.
Police quickly cordoned off the area and shut down the road after confirming the situation, bringing in the Bomb Disposal Unit to safely recover the device.
One passerby was reportedly injured during the process of defusing the bomb, according to reports from The Daily Star.
caption:
A bomb hidden in an umbrella? Police just defused an IED near Motijheel Metro Rail Station.

A bomb-like object, identified as an improvised explosive device (IED), was discovered beneath the Motijheel Metro Rail Station in Dhaka on Friday evening.

The device was hidden inside a red umbrella, designed to explode when the button was pressed. The CTTC bomb disposal team of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) neutralized the device.

Ansar members on duty at the metro station noticed the umbrella lying on the road near Shapla Chattar during a Rath Yatra procession.

Upon picking up the umbrella, Ansar members saw a red light flashing inside it, which immediately alerted them to the danger.

Police quickly cordoned off the area and shut down the road after confirming the situation, bringing in the Bomb Disposal Unit to safely recover the device.

One passerby was reportedly injured during the process of defusing the bomb, according to reports from The Daily Star.

headline_marked: Rooppur Nuclear Plant [[set for 'criticality' stage]] ahead of power generation
headline: Rooppur Nuclear Plant set for 'criticality' stage ahead of power generation
summary: The $12.65 billion facility has completed fuel loading and is awaiting final regulatory approval to begin its self-sustaining fission chain reaction.
details: The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has completed fuel loading and necessary tests, preparing to enter the 'criticality' stage—a vital milestone before electricity generation begins.
The plant is currently awaiting final approval from the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA), whose inspection team arrived at the facility for a review.
Criticality is the state where nuclear fuel sustains a self-supporting fission chain reaction. The process begins with a zero-power reaction, followed by low-power heating of water.
If all systems function as expected, the reactor will eventually reach higher power levels to generate steam, which drives turbines to produce electricity.
Experts note that it typically takes at least two months to reach final power generation from the first criticality stage.
The $12.65 billion project in Ishwardi, Pabna, is being built with Russian financial and technical support and features two VVER-1200 reactors designed for a combined 2,400 MW.
caption:
Bangladesh's first nuclear power plant is moving closer to generating electricity. The facility is now preparing for the 'criticality' stage.

The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant has completed fuel loading and necessary tests, preparing to enter the 'criticality' stage—a vital milestone before electricity generation begins.

The plant is currently awaiting final approval from the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA), whose inspection team arrived at the facility for a review.

Criticality is the state where nuclear fuel sustains a self-supporting fission chain reaction. The process begins with a zero-power reaction, followed by low-power heating of water.

If all systems function as expected, the reactor will eventually reach higher power levels to generate steam, which drives turbines to produce electricity.

Experts note that it typically takes at least two months to reach final power generation from the first criticality stage.

The $12.65 billion project in Ishwardi, Pabna, is being built with Russian financial and technical support and features two VVER-1200 reactors designed for a combined 2,400 MW.
